days.title: A sandbank in the open sea
days.lore: Nothing but water – and in the middle of it, a small sandbank. Tomorrow, the island begins.

days.title: The sandbank stretches north-east
days.lore: At low tide a new strip of sand rises off the north-east coast, and the sandbank is a little less alone.

days.title: The first grass on the western dunes
days.lore: Between the dunes, sheltered from the wind, a first patch of green grass takes root in the sand.

days.title: A sapling in the young meadow
days.lore: In the middle of the new grass a single sapling unfolds its first leaves, already leaning a little away from the sea wind.

days.title: A gull lands on the north-east shore
days.lore: A grey gull drifts in on the morning wind, folds its wings on the new sand and decides, for now, to stay.

days.title: New sand off the south-east coast
days.lore: Overnight the tide leaves a fresh crescent of sand in the south-east, and the gull walks its whole length before breakfast.

days.title: The meadow crosses to the eastern dunes
days.lore: The grass creeps east overnight, and now the sapling stands at the edge of a meadow two tiles wide.

days.title: A sandy point in the south-west
days.lore: In the south-west a low sandy point slips out of the water, and the waves begin to curl around it in a new way.

days.title: A sandbar in the north-west
days.lore: A pale sandbar surfaces off the north-west coast, still wet and shining, and the gull is the first to leave footprints on it.

days.title: The first stone on the south-west point
days.lore: On the south-west point a dark stone breaks through the sand, and the waves now have something to talk to.

days.title: The north shore reaches out
days.lore: On the north side a broad tongue of sand rises at dawn, and from its tip the whole small island can be seen at once.

days.title: Grass on the north-western dunes
days.lore: The meadow spreads north-west across the dunes, and the sand there now holds the evening dew a little longer.

days.title: The north coast grows wider
days.lore: Beside yesterday's grass a new strip of sand rises off the north coast, and the small island stretches a little further toward the cold.

days.title: Green on the north-eastern dunes
days.lore: The grass finds the north-eastern dunes, and now a small green field lies at the island's centre, ringed by sand on every side.

days.title: The first house in the meadow
days.lore: In the north-eastern meadow a small house with a grass roof appears, its one window turned toward the sapling and the sea.

days.title: Maren, the first islander
days.lore: Maren, a storyteller, moves into the house in the meadow and spends her first evening telling the gull how the sandbank became an island.

days.title: A lighthouse on the south-western rocks
days.lore: On the dark stone of the south-west point a small white lighthouse rises, and tonight its first beam sweeps slowly over the water.

days.title: Tove comes to keep the light
days.lore: Tove arrives to keep the new lighthouse, shares the meadow house with Maren, and climbs the stairs each dusk to wake the lamp.

days.title: A second tree in the north-western meadow
days.lore: In the north-western meadow a second young tree takes hold, so the first sapling no longer stands alone against the autumn wind.

days.title: Sand gathers in the north-west corner
days.lore: A curl of sand settles into the north-west corner, and from Tove's lamp the island's outline looks a little rounder each night.

days.title: A small jetty on the east coast
days.lore: A few weathered planks reach into the water off the east coast, and the first jetty waits quietly for a boat to tie up.

days.title: A boat at the east jetty
days.lore: A small blue boat now rocks beside the east jetty, its rope tied in a careful knot, and the planks no longer wait alone.

days.title: A garden beside the meadow house
days.lore: Maren and Tove dig a small garden beside their house, and the first rows of autumn seeds go into the dark, damp soil.

days.title: New sand in the north-east
days.lore: A fresh bank of sand rises in the north-east, and from the new boat Tove can now trace the whole curve of the shore.

days.title: A sandbar below the south coast
days.lore: Below the south coast a low sandbar surfaces at dawn, and the lighthouse beam now finds a little more shore on every turn.

days.title: Grass reaches toward the lighthouse
days.lore: The meadow creeps south toward the lighthouse, and on her way to the lamp each evening Tove now walks on soft grass.

days.title: The first field by the lighthouse
days.lore: On the new grass near the lighthouse Maren and Tove turn the first field, and the furrows lie straight and dark in the low autumn sun.

days.title: The south shore widens
days.lore: Beside the southern sandbar a second strip of sand rises, and the low tide now leaves a wide pale beach below the lighthouse.

days.title: Grass beside the first field
days.lore: The grass spreads beside the new field, and the island's green heart now reaches almost to the southern beach.

days.title: A third tree by the field
days.lore: A third young tree takes root at the edge of the field, where its leaves will one day shade the furrows on warm afternoons.

days.title: A second house on the north shore
days.lore: On the north shore a second small house goes up, its door facing the meadow, ready for whoever the boat brings next.

days.title: Ilka the farmer arrives by boat
days.lore: Ilka steps off the little boat with a sack of seed, moves into the north shore house, and walks straight out to see the field.

days.title: A well between the two houses
days.lore: The three islanders dig a stone well near the north-east shore, and the first bucket comes up cold, clear and only a little salty.

days.title: The first path to the well
days.lore: Daily trips for water wear a narrow path from the north shore house to the well, and the sand there is now packed firm by footsteps.
